### Context

A timing trace showed two four-minute passes over the code with identical file lists. Giving the first pass's results to the summary removed the second pass. Nothing was blocked.

### What is broken

The automatic build check spends its last four minutes doing no new work. It repeats a scan it has already finished.

### Why it is broken

The automatic check first scans the code for rule violations. The step that writes the final summary then scans the same code again instead of reusing that list. A trial that reused the first list finished four minutes sooner and produced the same summary.

### How to fix it

Give the summary step the list from the first scan instead of starting a second scan. Each run would finish about four minutes sooner with unchanged output. Choose hotfix because the fix changes only one place in the code.

1. [ ] Brainstorm now - /skill:brainstorming with this evidence as the seed.

3. [ ] Respond to reporter only.

gauntlet: gate=chase-bug/verdict-menu recommended=2

### Context

Browser inspection showed the letter "z" drawn in a different font. A trial with a complete font kept the heading inside its card. Nothing was blocked.

### What is broken

Slide headings that contain the letter "z" spill past the edge of their card.

### Why it is broken

The chosen heading font has no drawing for the letter "z". The browser fills that one letter from a wider substitute font. This widens the heading from 280 to 312 pixels on a 300-pixel card. With a complete font, the same heading stays at 280 pixels.

### How to fix it

Replace the heading font file with a complete version that includes "z". Leave the card width unchanged. The change is small, but the font file is kept outside this project. This project's tests cannot check a font stored elsewhere, so the change needs the font's owner. Choose brainstorm because that coordination comes before any change.

Pick one:

```text
1. [ ] File a ticket - /skill:shape-ticket, seeded with this evidence.
2. [x] Brainstorm now - /skill:brainstorming with this evidence as the seed. [recommended]
3. [ ] Implement hotfix now - follow hotfix.md; add "as a PR" for a PR.
4. [ ] Finish with rendered summary.

not eligible: predicate 6 - the existing test harness cannot verify the changed external font
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves plain-reader from fails to holds: Before leaned on unexplained shorthand ("CI job", "the lint step's results") and, in the font case, never said the fix leaves the card width alone, so a reader who did not open the citation could not reconstruct the whole mechanism; After renames those pieces by their actions ("the automatic build check", "scans the code for rule violations", "the step that writes the final summary") and states "Leave the card width unchanged" explicitly. The sectioned shape stays comfortably under the 180-word cap (roughly 145 and 150 words including headings), each section is a single paragraph with no stray bullets, the menus and eligibility lines are byte-for-byte equivalent in structure, and both gates still end at the closing fence. Nothing regressed; if anything, keep an eye on the dropped citations - After omits `tools/check-job.mjs:73` and `slides/title.css:41` entirely, which is permitted by the "only when useful to open" rule, but for the hotfix case the fixer's next action is literally opening that call site, so appending the identifier after the "one place in the code" claim would satisfy the trailing-citation guidance without hurting readability.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After improves on Before in two places: the sectioned contract made the second report state the fix as the font rather than the card width (Before never contrasted the two, so a reader could not tell why the card was left alone), and dropping the trailing 'Prior-report search completed...' line means both gates now end at the eligibility line, which Before violated by appending housekeeping after it. Nothing regressed: both reports stay well under 180 words, every section is a single paragraph, the menus keep their row counts, recommendation marks, last rows, and the predicate-6 naming. Two small wording risks worth tightening in the After contract: the CP1 eligibility line lost 'six' ('all predicates pass'), which is still fine for menu-intact but weaker than Before's explicit count, and the menu fence places the eligibility line outside the code block, which is permitted by ends-at-envelope but should be stated as the intended shape so future outputs don't drift the eligibility line inside the fence or add text after it. Keep the instruction that nothing follows the eligibility line, and consider requiring the eligibility line to echo the predicate count so the gate text matches hotfix.md's six-predicate vocabulary.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally satisfies plain-reader: the second Before report compressed the fix to "swaps in a complete font" and never said the card width stays as it is, so a reader could not tell from the text that the remedy was the font rather than the card; After's How-to-fix section states "leave the card width alone" explicitly, names the summary step and heading font by role, keeps citations trailing in parentheses, and stays unfenced with no arrow chains. Both After reports land around 115-125 words from first heading to Pick one:, each section is a single paragraph, Context is two lines of repro and blocked-check status, menus are byte-identical in structure to Before (three rows / four rows, correct recommended row, correct last row, eligibility lines naming predicate 6), and nothing follows the eligibility fence. The one soft spot worth a wording nudge in the contract: After's closing because-clause leans on "every predicate passes" and "predicate 6" without ever saying in everyday words what a predicate is; a line such as "one of the six hotfix checks fails: this repository's tests cannot verify the external font" would keep the plain-reader fact robust across cases where the eligibility line is the only place the term appears.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: both gates use the fixed What is broken / Why it is broken / How to fix it headings, each section is a single paragraph, the mechanisms are named by role with citations trailing, and each third section closes with the recommended pick plus one because-clause while the menus and eligibility lines are untouched. The only fact that moved is ends-at-envelope, and it moved in After's favor: Before appended a 'Prior-report search completed ... baseline checks were clean' housekeeping line after the eligibility line on both gates, whereas After stops at the eligibility line. That improvement likely comes from the 'standalone and concise' framing plus the explicit 'end the gate's third section with the recommended pick' instruction, which left no slot for trailing status; if you want to make it durable, add a sentence such as 'The eligibility line is the last line of the gate; search and baseline results belong inside Context or Why it is broken, never after the menu.' Two minor tightening notes: After's checkpoint 1 eligibility line says 'all predicates pass' rather than 'all six', and checkpoint 2 drops the 'other five predicates pass' clause from the not-eligible line—both still satisfy menu-intact, but a phrase like 'name the failed predicate and the count passing' would keep that detail without adding words to the report body.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After keeps every fact Before kept while delivering the sectioned contract. Both After gates use the fixed headings, each section is a single paragraph, Context stays at two evidence lines, word counts land well under 180, the citation trails the claim, and the menus and eligibility lines are unchanged and terminal. Two small points to watch as you tighten the wording: the first After report's because-clause says 'every predicate passes' and the second leans on 'needs that coordination' without naming predicate 6 in the body, so if the contract wants the gate's third section to be readable without the eligibility line, prefer a because-clause like 'because it touches one call site and all six hotfix checks pass' / 'because the font lives outside this repo and its tests cannot verify it (predicate 6)'. Also note After's menu seeds say 'with this evidence' rather than 'with the above'; harmless here, but keep the menu text fixed if any downstream check compares it literally.

The sectioned What is broken / Why it is broken / How to fix it shape reads plainly, each section is a single paragraph, citations trail the claims they support, both reports stay well under 180 words, and the menus match the expected row counts, recommendations, and eligibility statements (Checkpoint 2 names predicate 6 and the unverifiable external font).
